title: deployment conductivity heatmap and weekly run scripts (apr 2026) - draft
content:
Purpose
------
This is a working sketch: combine a deployment conductivity (traffic + dependency) heatmap with a compact weekly-run script set for on-call and release engineers. Goal: reduce surprise slowdowns during small-to-medium rollouts by making handoffs and throttles operationally obvious.

High-level objectives
- Surface the likely "conductivity" (how changes propagate under varying traffic patterns) across frontdoor -> router -> runtime -> cache -> kv-store lanes.
- Provide a recommended 3-week run cadence (warmup, steady, wind-down) with explicit smoke scripts.
- Bake-in quick rollback thresholds and immediate mitigations (traffic throttle, fallback model routing).
- Deliver a copyable checklist for rotation leads and oncall.

Methodology / how the heatmap is built
- Inputs: recent 30-day p95/p99 latencies by component, region traffic mix, failure correlation events (from the last 12 months).
- Scoring rules: conductivity = weighted sum(throughput elasticity, dependency fan-out, recent incident correlation). We use a 0-1 normalized score per lane, then bucket into Low/Medium/High.
- Visualization notes: rows are components (ingest, router, runtime, kv-read, kv-write, storage-write), columns are scenarios (normal, surge, degraded-edge, cold-start), cells are Low/Med/High with short rationale.

Quick heatmap summary (annotated)
- ingest | normal: Low — autoscaling handles baseline; normal p99 ~80ms.
- router  | surge: High — previous surge events show amplified backpressure to runtime. Avoid large model swaps during 08:00-10:00 PT.
- runtime | cold-start: Medium — large model cold-start increases p99 by ~400ms, but continuous batching mitigates for small RPS.
- kv-write | degraded-edge: High — write latency correlates with cascading retries; implement write-buffer throttle.

Weekly run cadence (3-week example)
Week 0 (preflight, day -7 to -1):
- Run subset of smoke scripts against staging (see scripts below).
- Canary plan: allocate 1-2% traffic for model variant A/B for 12h.
- Preflight checklist (owners): config, infra, db migrations reviewed (owner: @Ravi).
- Dry-run: simulate 3x normal traffic in a sandbox for 30 minutes. Capture telemetry snapshot.

Week 1 (warmup, day 0 to 7):
- Canary start: 1% -> 5% over first 24h, monitor latencies and error rates.
- Run smoke scripts on-hourly cadence for first 12h, then every 3h.
- Oncall: escalate threshold if p99 increases >40% or error-rate >0.8% (owner: rotation lead).

Week 2 (steady ramp, day 8 to 14):
- Ramp to 20% over 48h if metrics stable.
- Run full smoke run once per 12h.
- Observe non-functional regressions (cost per token, tail latency).

Week 3 (wind-down and postmortem prep, day 15 to 21):
- Pause ramp; monitor for 72h.
- Collect samples for quality evals; snapshot KV cache hit rates.
- Draft release notes (see section).

Preflight checklist (compact)
- [ ] Release manifest uploaded and pinned in release bucket (owner).
- [ ] Model hashes and variant mappings confirmed.
- [ ] Infra capacity reservations confirmed for Dedicated pools.
- [ ] Canary routing policy uploaded to console; fallback routes defined.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards linked in the release brief.
- [ ] Pager runbook updated with new alert thresholds and responsible engineers.

Smoke scripts (copy-and-run)
- smoke-basic.sh: 200 short text generation calls at target concurrency 5/region, assert HTTP 200, assert mean latency < 250ms.
- smoke-coldstart.sh: trigger runtime cold-start by clearing model cache on a single node and sending 30 parallel requests; measure p95/p99.
- smoke-kv-failure.sh: inject kv-read error (circuit-breaker) in staging and assert runtime uses degraded path without >2% error propagation.
- smoke-routing-fallback.sh: simulate node pool drain and ensure router failover to fallback variant within TTFB SLA.

Run script cadence (practical)
- On deploy: run smoke-basic, smoke-routing-fallback.
- After 2h: run smoke-coldstart, smoke-kv-failure.
- Nightly for first 7 days: smoke-basic at 03:00 PT and 15:00 PT.

Rollback thresholds & immediate mitigations
- Immediate rollback if: sustained error-rate >1.5% for 10 minutes, or p99 > 2x baseline for 15 minutes.
- Soft mitigation steps (ordered): 1) throttle to 50% of new model traffic, 2) switch router to fallback model variant, 3) reduce max tokens to 256 for affected route, 4) if unresolved -> full rollback.

Release notes (draft)
- Title: runtime: small-model-cache-improvements (2026-04)
- Summary: incremental optimizations to KV cache eviction and routing failover behavior aimed at reducing tail latency for multi-shard workloads.
- Impact: expected <5% average cost reduction on long-tail prompts; measurable p99 reductions on heavy batched workloads in EU-West region.
- Rollout plan: staged canary (1% -> 20%) over 14 days. Auto-fallback to previous classifier on error.
- Known limitations: doesn't change cold-start times for models > 20B; observe increased write contention in synthetic high-write KV benchmarks.

Open questions / notes to self
- Need a deterministic way to map heatmap "cells" back to owning decks in console; maybe a new tag in model metadata? (Janelle to prototype)
- Validate that cost-per-token telemetry has the same sampling rate across regions; discrepancy noted in EU-West (Tomás assigned).
- Consider adding a small synthetic workload that exercises large-kernel attention paths to catch rare slowdowns.

Action items before next sync
- @Ravi: finalize canary traffic ramp knobs and update PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842) — due 2026-04-12.
- @Janelle: prototype model metadata tag -> heatmap link (Confluence draft link in linked_artifacts) — due 2026-04-16.
- @Tomás: run cross-region cost-per-token sampling check and report differences.
- Owner (Ava): integrate this doc into the release brief and add the smoke scripts to the release-artifacts bucket.

Appendix: quick comms blurb for stakeholders
- "We're deploying a modest KV cache eviction change next week. We'll run a 2-week staged rollout with automatic fallback; immediate rollback thresholds are set. Expect negligible user-visible change in most regions; core improvement targets p99 for heavy batched workloads in EU-West."

Draft release note footer (for changelog)
- Author: Ava Martinez (eng-release-engineering)
- Contact: ava@redwood-inference.com
- Related tickets: JIRA RED-3981, PR #842

---
Notes: this is intentionally compact — intended to be pasted into a release brief. Keep edits light and call out anything that would change rollback thresholds or add infra reservations.
